title: The brothers' plan
hookLine: the brothers, jealous of their father's love, plot to be rid of Yusuf
last: NOT EVERY DREAM IS FOR TELLING.

cards: Anyone with a sibling knows the math. Who got the bigger slice. Who got to sit in front.
Whose drawing went on the fridge. It sounds petty written down, but it lives deep, and some families carry it for fifty years. Ya'qub has twelve sons.

Two of them, Yusuf and his younger brother, are the sons of the wife he lost, and the older ten can see where their father's eyes rest. The Qur'an never says they heard about the dream. It doesn't need to.
It lets us listen in on their conversation.

teach.b: The surah pauses first to tell us why we're listening: in Yusuf and his brothers there are signs for those who ask. This isn't only their family; it's everyone's. Then the brothers talk.

teach.h: DEARER TO OUR FATHER THAN WE.
teach.b: Yusuf and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, and we are a strong group. Our father is plainly mistaken.
Then someone says it: kill Yusuf, or throw him out into some far land, so your father's face will be yours alone.
And after that, you can be righteous people. Listen to that last part. They're not only planning the wrong; they're planning the repentance.
Jealousy is clever like that. It doesn't just feel. It schedules.
Then one brother, the Qur'an doesn't name him, pulls them back from the worst: don't kill Yusuf. Throw him into the bottom of the well, and some travelers will pick him up. Still cruel.
But one voice made it less cruel, and that matters later.
The Arabic word for jealousy of this kind is hasad, wanting someone else's blessing taken from them.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in a hadith in Bukhari and Muslim: don't envy one another, don't hate one another, don't turn your backs on one another; be servants of Allah, brothers. And that closes a week of hard rooms.
Musa asking for an open chest. A gentle word to Pharaoh. The magicians.
The sea. A golden calf. A boy's dream.
And now brothers in a huddle, making plans.

how: Muslims are taught to guard against hasad, envy, and many say masha'Allah or pray for blessing on others when they see something good in someone else's life.

o: anger at a father who plays favorites openly
admiration that makes you want to work harder
envy: wanting someone else's blessing taken from them

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: dearer to our father than we
kill him, or send him far away
not kill: the bottom of the well

s: the brothers say they're plotting because of the dream
they never mention it. what they name is their father's love: Yusuf and his brother are dearer to our father than we.
the brothers planned to be righteous after getting rid of Yusuf
they said: after that, you can be righteous people.
all the brothers wanted to kill Yusuf
one of them said: don't kill him. throw him into the well.

games.q: you're one of Yusuf's older brothers. the others are saying: kill Yusuf. what do you say?
o: go along with it; you're outnumbered.
don't kill him. throw him into the well, and some travelers will pick him up.
games.why: one unnamed brother said: don't kill him; the well instead. still cruel, but one voice made it less cruel.

practice: Think of someone whose life you've felt a pinch about lately, a friend's promotion, a sibling who seems to get the easy road, a stranger's vacation photos, and let the feeling come up without arguing with it.

Name it softly, the way you'd name a cloud: that's jealousy; not I'm a terrible person, just there it is, and watch whether it's already making plans, even small ones. If you pray, you can ask for good for that person.

wordCard.voice: Hasad, envy: what drove the brothers to plot against Yusuf, and plan to be righteous people afterward.

orig.note: Arabic: envy — wanting someone else's blessing taken from them. the word isn't in this scene, but it names what drives it.

carryVoice: Your line: jealousy makes plans. One voice in the huddle still made it less cruel. Day fifty-six, and a week complete.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6065; Sahih Muslim 2559 (do not envy one another... be servants of Allah, brothers)
